convention.name: module_header_comment
convention.rule: Every CREATE COMPUTE MODULE and CREATE FILTER MODULE must start with a structured header comment documenting the node name, description, and version history.

convention.name: copy_procedures
convention.rule: Always include CopyMessageHeaders() and CopyEntireMessage() helper procedures in every Compute/Filter module — they are used in nearly every module.
Call CopyEntireMessage() at the top of Main() before making changes, or call CopyMessageHeaders() when only copying headers and constructing a new body.

convention.name: broker_schema
convention.rule: Every ESQL file must start with BROKER SCHEMA declaration matching the Java package path of the file. Example: BROKER SCHEMA com.company.esb
Use a PATH statement when referencing procedures from other ESQL files in a shared library: PATH com.company.esb.common;

convention.name: variable_declaration
convention.rule: Declare all local variables at the top of a function/procedure with DECLARE.
Use SHARED variables (DECLARE x SHARED CHARACTER '') for state shared across multiple messages — but use with caution as they persist across message processing.
Use EXTERNAL variables (DECLARE x EXTERNAL CHARACTER 'default') for User-Defined Properties (UDPs) that can be configured per-environment in properties files.

convention.name: null_handling
convention.rule: Always use COALESCE() when reading values that might be NULL to avoid null propagation in string operations.
Use FIELDTYPE() to test whether a field exists before reading it. Example: IF FIELDTYPE(Environment.Variables.myField) IS NULL THEN
Use EXISTS() to check for the presence of an element: IF EXISTS(OutputRoot.HTTPRequestHeader.MyHeader[]) THEN

convention.name: error_handling
convention.rule: For SOAP services, return HTTP 500 with a SOAP Fault in the error response. Set OutputRoot.HTTPResponseHeader."X-Original-HTTP-Status-Code" = 500.
For JSON/REST services, return HTTP 500 with a JSON error body.
Always include a timeout handler that returns a meaningful error to the caller.

convention.name: propagate_usage
convention.rule: Use PROPAGATE TO TERMINAL 'terminalName' DELETE NONE when propagating to multiple terminals and the message must be preserved for subsequent propagations.
Use RETURN FALSE to suppress default propagation after explicit PROPAGATEs.
Use RETURN TRUE to let the message flow to the default 'out' terminal.

convention.name: environment_tree
convention.rule: Use the Environment message tree to pass state between nodes in a flow. Prefix all custom environment variables under Environment.Variables to keep them organized. Example: Environment.Variables.ServiceContext.PolicyNumber
Use Environment.Variables.WMB.Audit for audit-related fields, following the established pattern in the shared services library.
Clean up large data from Environment when no longer needed to avoid memory waste.

convention.name: database_access
convention.rule: Always use parameterised queries (PASSTHRU with ? placeholders) rather than string concatenation to build SQL — prevents SQL injection.
Declare an EXIT HANDLER FOR SQLSTATE to catch database errors gracefully.
Cache database lookups in SHARED ROW variables when the data changes infrequently, with a timestamp-based expiry mechanism.

convention.name: naming
convention.rule: Message flow files: ServiceName_Flow.msgflow or ServiceName_SubFlow.subflow
Subflow files: FunctionName_SubFlow.subflow
Node labels in a flow: NodeFunction_NodeType. Example: ValidateInput_Compute, RouteToBackend_Filter, ErrorHandler_SubFlow
ESQL module names must match the node label they are associated with.

convention.name: error_handler_pattern
convention.rule: Every service flow must have an error handler subflow connected to the catch terminal of the input node AND the catch/failure terminals of HTTP Request nodes.
Use a shared Error_SubFlow from the library rather than duplicating error handling logic in every flow.

convention.name: audit_pattern
convention.rule: Use FlowOrder nodes to sequence audit logging so audit messages are sent before and after key processing steps without blocking the main flow.
Connect audit subflow outputs without any downstream nodes — audit messages are fire-and-forget via MQ to an audit queue.

convention.name: structure
convention.rule: Create separate properties files for each environment: DEV.properties, QA.properties, UAT.properties, PROD.properties
Property keys follow the format: BrokerSchema.FlowName#NodeLabel.propertyName

convention.name: environment_differences
convention.rule: Never hardcode environment-specific values (URLs, queue names, email addresses) in ESQL — always use EXTERNAL variables configured via properties files.
Performance tuning properties (additionalInstances, timeouts) must differ between environments — DEV should have lower values than PROD.

convention.name: when_to_use_java
convention.rule: Use JavaCompute nodes for: complex string manipulation (byte-level operations), file system operations, calling third-party Java libraries, UUID generation, sending emails via JavaMail.
Prefer ESQL for: message transformation, routing, database access, and simple string operations — it is simpler to maintain.

convention.name: java_esql_bridge
convention.rule: To call Java from ESQL, declare the Java method as an ESQL external procedure: CREATE PROCEDURE MyJavaProc(IN param CHARACTER) LANGUAGE JAVA EXTERNAL NAME "com.company.esb.MyClass.myMethod";
Java methods called from ESQL must be public static and use supported types (String, int, long, float, double, MbElement for tree references).

pre_development.item: Requirements understood: protocol, format, transformation, error handling

during_development.item: Every .msgflow has correct xmi:type from ace-bob skill (not copied from examples)
BROKER SCHEMA declaration matches file path
CopyMessageHeaders() / CopyEntireMessage() included in every module
COALESCE() used for all nullable field reads
Error handler connected to all catch/failure terminals
EXTERNAL variables used for all environment-specific values

before_completion.item: All four environment properties files created and populated
Error paths tested with invalid inputs
No hardcoded environment-specific values in ESQL
No client-specific names used in code (use generic names like ServiceConsumer, BackendSystem, IntegrationService)
